[ ] Create a convolution layer with `nn.Conv2D` using 3 channels as input, and a single one for output. ::: {#ad1b7a4a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import torch.nn as nn conv_1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=1, kernel_size=7, padding=0, bias=True) x, _ = next(iter(cifar_train_dl)) fx = conv_1(x) ``` ::: ::: {#61b947a9 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("Input:", type(x), x.dtype, x.shape, x.min(), x.max()) print("Output:", type(fx), fx.dtype, fx.shape, fx.min(), fx.max()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Input: torch.float32 torch.Size([128, 3, 32, 32]) tensor(0.) tensor(1.) Output: torch.float32 torch.Size([128, 1, 26, 26]) tensor(-0.8468, grad_fn=) tensor(0.1861, grad_fn=) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-warning} The convolution layer is initialized with random values, so the results will vary. ::: --- ## Exercise: Visualize the effect of the convolution operation - [ ] Create a convolution layer with `nn.Conv2D` using 3 channels as input, and a single one for output. ::: {#76280ce7 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = [5, 5] fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2) ax[0].imshow(x[0].permute(1, 2, 0)) ax[1].imshow(fx.detach()[0, 0], cmap="gray") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](DL_image_analysis_1_2_files/figure-revealjs/cell-5-output-1.png){} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} By default, outputs from PyTorch modules are tracked for back-propagation. To visualize it with `matplotlib` we have to `.detach()` the tensor first. ::: --- ## Exercise: Visualize the effect of the convolution operation - [ ] Visualize the weights of the convolution layer. ::: {#aae7ef67 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} conv_1.weight.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` torch.Size([1, 3, 7, 7]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3ad9a3b1 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2) ax[0, 0].imshow(conv_1.weight.detach()[0, 0], cmap="gray") ax[0, 1].imshow(conv_1.weight.detach()[0, 1], cmap="gray") ax[1, 0].imshow(conv_1.weight.detach()[0, 2], cmap="gray") ax[1, 1].set_axis_off() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](DL_image_analysis_1_2_files/figure-revealjs/cell-7-output-1.png){} ::: ::: --- ## Exercise: Visualize the effect of the convolution operation - nn.Conv2d(in_channels=6, out_channels=16, kernel_size=5, bias=True), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2), nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(in_features=16*5*5, out_features=120, bias=True), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(in_features=120, out_features=84, bias=True), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(in_features=84, out_features=100, bias=True), ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note} Pooling layers are used to downsample feature the model to classify images from CIFAR-100. ::: {#a5d1da75 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} import torch.optim as optim num_epochs = 10 train_loss = [] val_loss = [] if torch.cuda.is_available(): lenet_clf.cuda() optimizer = optim.SGD(lenet_clf.parameters(), lr=0.01) loss_fun = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() for e in range(num_epochs): train_loss_avg = 0 total_train_samples = 0 lenet_clf.train() for x, y in cifar_train_dl: optimizer.zero_grad() if torch.cuda.is_available(): x = x.cuda() y_hat = lenet_clf( x ).cpu() loss = loss_fun(y_hat, y) train_loss_avg += loss.item() * len(x) total_train_samples += len(x) loss.backward() optimizer.step() train_loss_avg /= total_train_samples train_loss.append(train_loss_avg) val_loss_avg = 0 total_val_samples = 0 lenet_clf.eval() with torch.no_grad(): for x, y in cifar_val_dl: if torch.cuda.is_available(): x = x.cuda() y_hat = lenet_clf( x ).cpu() loss = loss_fun(y_hat, y) val_loss_avg += loss.item() * len(x) total_val_samples += len(x) val_loss_avg /= total_val_samples val_loss.append(val_loss_avg) print(f"[Epoch {e}] Training loss: {train_loss_avg}, validation loss: {val_loss_avg}") ``` ::: {.cell-output val_acc_metric = Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=100) test_acc_metric = Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=100) train_acc_metric = Accuracy(task="multiclass", num_classes=100) with for x, y in cifar_val_dl: if torch.cuda.is_available(): x = x.cuda() y_hat = lenet_clf( x ).cpu() val_acc_metric(y_hat.softmax(dim=1), y) val_acc = val_acc_metric.compute() for x, y in cifar_test_dl:
